read.sections.0.text.back: Every community needs water for drinking, cooking and washing. In many places, rivers give fresh water all year round. Farmers dig small canals to bring river water to their fields. When floods happen, the river leaves a layer of mud on the land, and this mud makes the soil fertile, so crops like wheat and rice grow well. Rivers also give fish to eat. That is why some of the first large settlements grew beside rivers. In ancient Egypt, people farmed along the Nile River, and in today's Iraq, people farmed between the Tigris River and the Euphrates River. The River Site in Riverlands has the same kind of flat, fertile land.
read.sections.0.text.source: Every community needs water to drink, cook and wash. In many places, a river gives fresh water all year. Farmers dig small canals to carry river water to their fields. When a river floods, it leaves a layer of mud on the land, and this mud makes the soil fertile, so crops like wheat and rice grow well. Rivers also give people fish to eat. That is why some of the first large settlements grew beside rivers. In ancient Egypt, people farmed along the Nile, and in today's Iraq, people farmed between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers. The River site in Riverlands has the same kind of flat, fertile land.

read.sections.0.simpler.back: Humans need water for drinking, cooking and washing. Rivers give water. Farmers bring river water to their fields. Sometimes floods happen. Then the river leaves mud on the land. Mud makes the soil fertile. Crops grow well there. People also catch fish in the river. So, many early settlements grew beside rivers. One example is Egypt, beside the Nile River. The River Site on the map also has fertile soil.
read.sections.0.simpler.source: People need water to drink, cook and wash. A river gives water. Farmers take river water to their fields. Sometimes a river floods. Then it leaves mud on the land. The mud makes the soil fertile. Crops grow well there. People also catch fish in rivers. So many early settlements grew next to rivers. One example is Egypt, by the Nile River. The River site on the map has fertile land too.

read.sections.1.heading.back: Rivers help people travel and trade
read.sections.1.heading.source: Rivers help people travel and trade

read.sections.1.text.back: A river can work like a road made of water. In the past, before there were trucks or trains, boats could carry heavy goods, such as grain, wood and cloth, more easily than people or animals. Cities often grew in places where boats stopped so that people could buy and sell. Many important cities today are still located beside rivers. Bangkok in Thailand is located beside the Chao Phraya River, and Kinshasa, a big city in Central Africa, is located beside the Congo River. In Riverlands, boats can stop at the River Site. A city there could trade with other cities upstream and downstream on the river.
read.sections.1.text.source: Rivers can work like roads made of water. Long ago, before there were trucks or trains, boats could carry heavy goods, like grain, wood and cloth, more easily than people or animals could. Towns often grew at places where boats stopped so that people could buy and sell. Many important cities today still sit on rivers. Bangkok in Thailand is on the Chao Phraya River, and Kinshasa, a large city in Central Africa, is on the Congo River. In Riverlands, boats can stop at the River site. A town there could trade with other towns up and down the river.

read.sections.1.simpler.back: Boats can move on rivers. In the past, there were no trucks or trains. Boats carried heavy goods, such as rice and wood. People bought and sold these goods in cities. So, cities grew in places where boats stopped. Many big cities are still beside rivers. Bangkok is located beside a river in Thailand. Kinshasa is located beside the Congo River in Africa. On the map, boats can stop at the River Site.
read.sections.1.simpler.source: Boats can move on rivers. Long ago, there were no trucks or trains. Boats carried heavy goods, like rice and wood. People bought and sold these goods in towns. So towns grew where boats stopped. Many big cities are still on rivers. Bangkok is on a river in Thailand. Kinshasa is on the Congo River in Africa. On the map, boats can stop at the River site.

read.sections.2.text.note: Translator: 'Tall wooden legs' is translated as 'tiang kayu yang tinggi' (tall wooden stilts/posts), which is the natural Malay way to describe stilt houses. Check that this is fine.
read.sections.2.text.back: Living near a river also has risks. After heavy rain, a river can overflow, and water floods roads, fields and houses for a while. People who live beside rivers have found ways to be prepared. In some areas of Cambodia and Brazil, there are families who build houses on tall wooden posts, so that water can flow underneath. In other places, people build high earth banks along the river to stop water from coming in. Some cities were built on higher ground, like the Hill Site, but people have to carry water farther. No place is perfect, so a good choice compares the good points with the risks.
read.sections.2.text.source: Living near a river has risks too. After heavy rain, a river can flood, and water covers roads, fields and homes for a time. People who live by rivers have found ways to prepare. In parts of Cambodia and Brazil, some families build houses on tall wooden legs, so water can pass underneath. In other places, people build high banks of earth along the river to keep the water out. Some towns are built on higher ground, like the Hill site, but then people must carry water further. No place is perfect, so a good choice compares the benefits with the risks.

read.sections.2.simpler.back: Rivers can also bring problems. After a lot of rain, floods can happen. Water covers fields, roads and houses for a while. People look for ways to be prepared. Some families build houses on tall posts. So, water can flow under the house. Some cities build tall earth walls beside the river. Other cities are on hills. But people have to carry water from far away. Every place has good points and risks.
read.sections.2.simpler.source: Rivers can bring problems too. After a lot of rain, a river can flood. Water covers fields, roads and homes for a time. People find ways to get ready. Some families build houses on tall legs. Then water can go under the house. Some towns build high walls of earth by the river. Other towns are on a hill. But then people carry water a long way. Every place has good things and risks.

write.example.back: I would build the new city at the River Site. One reason is that its land is flat and fertile, so farmers can grow crops. Another reason is that boats can stop there, so people can trade goods with other cities. One problem that might happen is flooding in the rainy season. People could deal with this problem by building houses on tall posts. They could also prepare a safe place on the hill to use when the water rises.
write.example.source: I would build the new town at the River site. One reason is that the land is flat and fertile, so farmers can grow crops. Another reason is that boats can stop there, so people can trade goods with other towns. One problem could be floods in the rainy season. People could deal with this problem by building houses on tall legs. They could also keep a safe place on the hill for when the water is high.

watch.summary.back: This video is about Mesopotamia. This name means 'land between rivers'. It [is] a flat, fertile area between the Tigris River and the Euphrates River. Today, this land is located in Iraq, Syria and Kuwait. Its good land was very suitable for farming, so people farmed there for thousands of years. About 5,000 to 6,000 years ago, some farming villages developed into some of the first cities in the world. The people of these cities built large temples called ziggurats. They counted in groups of 60. That is why one hour has 60 minutes. They also invented one of the earliest kinds of writing. They pressed marks into wet clay. A king named Hammurabi ordered his laws to be written down. Many of these ideas are still used to this day.
watch.summary.source: This video is about Mesopotamia. The name means 'land between rivers'. It was a flat, fertile area between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers. Today this land is in Iraq, Syria and Kuwait. The good soil was great for farming, so people farmed there for thousands of years. About 5,000 to 6,000 years ago, some farming villages grew into some of the world's first cities. People in these cities built large temples called ziggurats. They counted in groups of 60. That is why an hour has 60 minutes. They also made one of the first kinds of writing. They pressed marks into wet clay. A king named Hammurabi had his laws written down. Many of these ideas are still used today.
